candidate.answerReason: Their combined painting rate is 1/5 + 1/7 rooms per hour. The total time t includes one hour without painting, so they work for t - 1 hours.

methods.label: Separate working time from elapsed time
methods.explanation:
Use one completed room as one unit of work. Doug paints \(1/5\) of the room per hour, and Dave paints \(1/7\) of the room per hour. Together their rate is
\[
\frac15+\frac17
\]
rooms per hour.

The total time \(t\) includes a one-hour lunch break, so their actual painting time is \(t-1\) hours, with \(t>1\). Rate times working time must equal one completed room. Therefore
\[
\boxed{\left(\frac15+\frac17\right)(t-1)=1},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses unit work rates and a simple equation relating rate, working time, and completed work.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task specifically assesses modeling a shared job by taking total work as 1. Division supplies each worker's hourly rate, and the rate-times-time relationship produces the equation after removing lunch from elapsed time. The general equation-modeling node is used only for forming the work equality.
